title: Patch: the web client's repeated blocks are written once
thread:
**Issue #5026 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #5026: Patch: the web client's repeated blocks are written once Opened by @squishy-squooby. ### Kind Architecture ### Why The audit that landed as #4905 ended with a scan for blocks of code that stand word for word in two places. On `main` at `7270e555` it finds 62 such runs in the client's non-test TypeScript under `apps/web/src` (windows of 12 or more lines, comments, blank lines and lone braces left out; the generated `wire/` files, the WebAssembly package and the per-card art recipes skipped). None was folded in #4905. The largest: | Files | Lines | |---|---| | `fx/motifs/names.ts` (8-38 and 50-80) | 31 | | `dungeon/store.ts:340-366` and `dungeon/test/fixtures.ts` (a fixture copying the store) | 27 | | `replay/OpenedReplay.tsx:45-70` and `duos/DuosReplay.tsx:240-265` | 26 | | `cards/proficiencySync.ts:97-122` and `cards/cardPicksSync.ts:161-186` | 23 | | `stats/model.ts` (38-56 and 83-101) | 19 | | `dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx` and `assault/fight/FightScreen.tsx` | 19, 14, 12, 12 | | `routes/practice.tsx:313-332` and `assault/AssaultPage.tsx:61-80` | 18 | | `game/deckbuilder/DeckHistory.tsx:102-126` and `DeckCosmeticsPicker.tsx:37-61` | 18 | | `cards/inspect/index.ts:17-34` and `cards/index.ts:43-60` | 18 | | `game/net.ts` and `duos/socket.ts` | 17, 14 | | `dungeon/fight/ArtifactTray.tsx:40-62` and `assault/fight/UpgradeTray.tsx:74-96` | 17 | | `fx/exits.ts:140-154` and `fx/entrances.ts:385-399` | 15 | | `cards/art/sceneKitGear.ts` and `sceneKitCraft.ts`; `sceneKitNature.ts` and `sceneKitInkCharacters.ts`; `sceneKitSpace.ts` and `sceneKitPlaces.ts`; `kitDraw.ts` and `procedural.ts` | 15, 13, 12, 12 | The rest are runs of 12 to 14 lines in `game/deckbuilder/` (`TrioEditor.tsx` and `DeckEditor.tsx`, `DeckDrag.tsx` and `game/drag/OptionDrag.tsx`), `collection/` (`CardCosmeticsView.tsx` and `AccountCosmeticTiles.tsx`), `duos/DuosBoard.tsx`, `dungeon/map/RewardScreens.tsx`, `routes/stats.tsx`, `routes/landing.tsx`, `routes/match.tsx` and `duos/DuosRoute.tsx`, `rank/RankCrest.tsx`, `game/drag/DragLayer.tsx` and `game/aim/OpponentAim.tsx`, `game/LanePick.tsx` and `game/GigaPlacement.tsx`, `daily/NotificationSettings.tsx` and `daily/DailyRoute.tsx`, `auth/UsernamePrompt.tsx` and `auth/ConsentPrompt.tsx`. The script under "How to list them" prints every run's lines. ### What to change Read each pair side by side and decide: - **Fold** it when one function, hook or component serves both sites and what renders and what is sent stay exactly the same: the same DOM, class names and test ids, the same order of effects and network calls. Both sites use it. The result is shorter and no harder to read. - **Leave** data tables, type declarations that merely look alike, re-export lists, and repeats where a shared form needs more parameters than the lines it saves. Say which in the pull request, with file and line. - A test fixture that copies product code imports it instead. - CLAUDE.md rules 7 and 9: the client enforces no rule and restates no engine or server number. - Any non-test change under `apps/web/src/cards/` is a card-visual change (R2529000) and needs a pending fragment with `--visual` and a player note (`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md`); nothing a card face renders may change. If that version is not worth it, leave the `cards/` pairs and say so. ### Acceptance - The pull request has a table of every run: folded into what, or left and why. - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web apps/edge apps/admin e2e`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck` and `typecheck:component` pass; CI's `web` and `e2e smoke` pass. - `cargo jackioh patches check` and `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` pass if `apps/web/src/cards/` changed. - The scan below, run again, lists only the runs the table says were left. ### How to list them ```bash python3 dups.py . 12 ts,tsx apps/web/src apps/edge apps/admin ```
dups.py ```python # Verbatim duplicate blocks in non-test source: windows of W normalized lines seen in 2+ places, # merged into maximal runs. Usage: dups.py ... import sys, os, re, hashlib, collections root, W, exts = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), tuple('.'+e for e in sys.argv[3].split(',')) dirs = sys.argv[4:] def norm(l): l = l.strip() if not l or l.startswith(('//', '/*', '*', '#[', '#!')) or l in ('{', '}', '};', '),', ')', '});', '],', ']', 'else {', '} else {'): return None return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', l) files = {} for d in dirs: for dp, dn, fs in os.walk(os.path.join(root, d)): if any(x in dp for x in ('/target', 'node_modules', '/tests', '/testkit', '/scripts/', '/pkg', '/generated', '/wire/', '/test/', '/__')): continue for f in fs: if not f.endswith(exts) or '.test.' in f or f.endswith('_test.go') or f.endswith('.d.ts'): continue p = os.path.join(dp, f); t = open(p, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read() if p.endswith('.rs'): m = re.search(r'^#\[cfg\(test\)\]\n(pub(\([a-z]+\))?\s+)?mod\s+\w+\s*\{', t, re.M) if m: t = t[:m.start()] lines = [(i+1, norm(l)) for i, l in enumerate(t.split('\n'))] files[os.path.relpath(p, root)] = [(i, n) for i, n in lines if n] seen = collections.defaultdict(list) for p, ls in files.items(): for k in range(len(ls) - W + 1): h = hashlib.md5('\n'.join(n for _, n in ls[k:k+W]).encode()).hexdigest() seen[h].append((p, k)) dup = {h: v for h, v in seen.items() if len(v) > 1} marks = collections.defaultdict(set) for h, v in dup.items(): for p, k in v: marks[p].add(k) runs = [] for p, ks in marks.items(): ks = sorted(ks); s = ks[0]; prev = ks[0] for k in ks[1:] + [None]: if k is None or k != prev + 1: ls = files[p]; a = ls[s][0]; b = ls[prev + W - 1][0] h = hashlib.md5('\n'.join(n for _, n in ls[s:s+W]).encode()).hexdigest() others = sorted({q for q, _ in dup[h] if q != p}) or [p + ' (itself)'] runs.append((prev - s + W, p, a, b, others)) if k is not None: s = k prev = k if k is not None else prev runs.sort(reverse=True) print(f'{len(runs)} duplicated runs, {sum(r[0] for r in runs)} normalized lines in them (each side counted)') for n, p, a, b, others in runs: print(f'{n:4} {p}:{a}-{b} ~ {", ".join(others[:2])}') ```
### Blocked by, part of Follow-up to #4905 (its handoff is on #4702). The Rust pairs are #5024 and #5025. The scheduled audit #5005 asks for duplicates in general in its part 2; this issue takes the client's listed pairs, so that audit can leave them. ````
